newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index up 2.93 pct, ends at day's high.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index up 2.93 pct, ends at day's high.

text.p: The Philippine stock market's main index closed 82.62 points, or 2.93 percent, up at 2,905.97 points on across-the-board buying led by property stocks, traders said.
"Following the run-up of Empire and Megaworld the past two days, people are turning their attention to oversold counters," said Raul Ruiz, vice-president at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities said foreign investors were seen back into the market as turnover was heavy at 3.2 billion pesos.
The main index breached the 2,850 initial resistance in early trade and pierced the next resistance level of 2,900 towards close.
In the broader market, gainers pounded losers 101 to 34. All indices rose.

"We all know it was the property sector that depressed the market and after their rise yesterday, people may have realised that their worries may be all over," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.

The Philippine's biggest property concern Ayala Land Inc ended 1.50 pesos up at 24 pesos while mass-housing firm Empire East Land Holdings continued raking gains for the third straight day ending 30 centavos higher at 4.0 pesos.
Index-linked Pilipino Telephone Corp, another oversold issue, ended 1.50 pesos higher at 11.50 pesos.

Magnum International Securities research head Mayenne Catimbang said some funds may be finding their way to the Philippines after the Dow's recent declines. Overnight, the Dow shed 42.07 points to 7,718.71.
BPI Securities Corp analyst Spencer Yap said after today's sharp gains he expected the market to take slight profits on Friday.
"We were technically ripe for an uptick. It looks like this is the start of a recovery but we have to look at second quarter earnings to say that indeed there is a reversal," said Yap.
